To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) associative strength accrued to a goal-box stimulus is not transferred to other nonrewarded stimuli, (b) nonrewarded goalbox placements can be used to produce a conditioned stimulus (CS) that is highly specific to that particular stimulus, and (c) the associative strength of the nonrewarded goal box is not transferred to the running stimulus.

(a) the associative strength of a conditioned stimulus (CS) is determined by the number of trials on which the CS is paired with an unconditioned stimulus (US), (b) associative strength is a function of the US, (c) associative strength generalizes from the CS to other stimuli that were present when the CS was paired with the US, and (d) associative strength is not affected by the US unless the US occurs during the CS.

(a) the nonrewarded goal box is a conditioned stimulus, (b) the nonrewarding of the goal box is an unconditioned stimulus, (c) the nonreward goal box is a stronger conditioned stimulus than the reward goal box, (d) nonrewarded running to the nonreward goal-box is a stronger conditioned response than rewarded running to the reward goal box.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of nonrewarded placements on the acquisition and retention of a running response.
the effects of nonrewarded placements into a goal-box on subsequent extinction performance in the runway.
the role of the nonrewarded goalbox in extinction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data are consistent with the view that nonrewarded goal box placements are not effective as unconditioned stimuli in the acquisition of conditioned responding.
the data indicate that the nonrewarded running stimulus is more effective in the acquisition of the running response than is the nonrewarded goal box stimulus.
the data are not consistent with the hypothesis of an associative strength gradient between stimuli associated with reward and stimuli associated with nonreinforced running.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nonrewarded goal box placements are more powerful than nonrewarded running in producing a resistance to extinction.
the associative strength acquired by the nonrewarded goal box placements is specific to that context.
the nonrewarded goal box is a unique conditioned stimulus that is not readily replaced by other nonrewarded stimuli.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the goal-box placement procedure can be used as a tool to investigate associative learning in a manner that is distinct from the more commonly employed running trials procedure.
associative strength accrued in the goal-box is specific to the goal-box and that the goal-box is a very powerful stimulus.
associative strength accrued in the goal box during the nonrewarded training was specific to the goal box.
